extracted.intended_audience: authors and peer reviewers of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses using the PRISMA 2020 checklist and related extensions; intended to help authors prepare complete reports and help peer reviewers verify essential reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 2020 27-item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A 27-item checklist addressing the introduction, methods, results and discussion sections of a systematic review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist covers items across the full manuscript (title, abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, funding). An expanded checklist is available that details reporting recommendations for each item/sub-item, with examples to help authors report completely.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 2020 12-item checklist for the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A 12-item checklist specifically addressing reporting in the abstract of a systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abstract checklist to ensure key elements are concisely reported in the abstract; examples and an expanded checklist provide detailed recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reporting of rationale, methods, and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should completely report why a systematic review was done, what methods were used, and what results were found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA provides guidance and examples to support full and transparent reporting of the review question/rationale, search and selection methods, data collection and synthesis methods, and the main findings and their interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript title should reflect that the study is a systematic review and/or meta-analysis and appropriately describe scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRISMA checklist includes title as a reporting item; titles should clearly identify the report as a systematic review (and meta-analysis, if applicable) to aid discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must contain key elements as specified by the 12-item abstract checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PRISMA abstract checklist to include objectives, eligibility criteria, information sources, key results, strengths/limitations, and conclusions; examples are provided in the expanded checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction sections should state the rationale and objectives of the review clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA items prompt authors to describe the review question(s), objectives, and context (why the review was needed) to situate the study for readers and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must be reported in sufficient detail to enable reproducibility (eligibility criteria, information sources, search strategy, selection process, data collection, risk of bias assessment, synthesis methods, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expanded checklist provides itemized guidance for each methodological element; transparent, reproducible descriptions of searches, screening, data extraction, and analysis are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should report study selection, characteristics of included studies, risk of bias assessments, and synthesis/findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA recommends using the flow diagram to show numbers of records screened and reasons for exclusions; present characteristics, results of individual studies, and any meta-analytic syntheses with measures of effect and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion should interpret results in context, discuss limitations (of evidence and review processes), and implications for practice and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should relate findings to existing knowledge, address strengths and limitations, and state implications and conclusions clearly as prompted by PRISMA items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and competing interests reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must disclose funding sources and any competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA explicitly includes funding in the checklist to ensure transparency about financial support and potential conflicts that could affect the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: A template flow diagram that documents the flow of information through the different phases of a systematic review (identification, screening, eligibility, included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template diagram and modify it as appropriate (e.g., for original vs updated reviews) to show numbers of records at each stage and reasons for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PRISMA extensions where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply PRISMA extensions developed for different review types or aspects when relevant (e.g., scoping reviews, protocols, abstracts, IPD, network meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy, equity, searching).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate extension (PRISMA-ScR, PRISMA-P, PRISMA-A, PRISMA-IPD, PRISMA-NMA, PRISMA-DTA, PRISMA-Equity, PRISMA for Searching) to supplement the core checklist with domain-specific reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-ScR (Scoping Reviews) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension to facilitate transparent reporting of scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA-ScR when the review is a scoping review to follow items tailored to scoping review objectives and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-P (Protocols) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension for reporting protocols of systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA-P to prepare and report review protocols, ensuring prespecified methods are transparently documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-A (Abstracts) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension providing the 12-item abstract checklist and recommendations for abstract reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA-A to structure abstracts for clear communication of objectives, methods, results and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-IPD (Individual Participant Data) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension addressing reporting requirements for systematic reviews and meta-analyses of individual participant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When IPD are used, follow PRISMA-IPD for items specific to data collection, integrity, and analysis at the participant level.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-NMA (Network Meta-analyses) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension to support reporting of network meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA-NMA where network meta-analysis methods and results require specialized reporting (e.g., network geometry, inconsistency).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-DTA (Diagnostic Test Accuracy) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension for reporting systematic reviews of diagnostic test accuracy studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PRISMA-DTA for items specific to diagnostic accuracy (index tests, reference standards, accuracy measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-Equity extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension to incorporate equity considerations into reporting of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA-Equity to ensure reporting addresses health equity-relevant questions, populations and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA for Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension focused on reporting search methods and strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this extension to transparently report information sources, search strategies, databases, dates, and search-related methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use of PRISMA as a structured rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers can use the PRISMA checklist as a structured rubric to verify that essential reporting items are present and appropriately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing systematic reviews and meta-analyses, check each PRISMA item/sub-item and the abstract checklist; use the expanded checklist and examples to assess completeness and transparency of reporting.
